title: First Women University — History
content: Shaheed Benazir Bhutto Women University Peshawar is the first public sector women university in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

title: Benazir Bhutto — History
content: The university was named to honor Benazir Bhutto and other women of Pakistan who contributed to women empowerment and national development.

title: Inauguration — History
content: The campus was inaugurated on 1 September 2004 by the Chief Minister of KPK.

title: Law — History
content: The university was established under the Frontier Women University Act 2004, later published in 2005 as a provincial act.

title: Vice Chancellor — History
content: The first Vice Chancellor, Prof. Dr. Syeda Farhana Jahangir, was appointed on 10 June 2005.

title: Camp Office — History
content: The university initially operated from the Department of Psychology at the University of Peshawar and became functional in a college hostel building.

title: Departments — History
content: In February 2006, academic activities started with 8 departments including Arabic, Psychology, Computer Science, Islamiat, Mathematics, Statistics, Economics, and English with 240 students.

title: Infrastructure — History
content: In 2007, land of 400 kanals was allotted but initially occupied, and a PC-I project worth 456 million rupees was approved.

title: New Programs — History
content: New disciplines like Bioinformatics and Microbiology were introduced in 2007 along with a Clinical Psychology diploma and psychotherapeutic clinic.

title: Women Development — History
content: Women Development Center and Education Department were established in 2008, introducing B.Ed, diplomas, and certificate programs.

title: Mphil Phd — History
content: MPhil and PhD programs started in English, Islamiat, and Psychology. Several colleges were affiliated and international MoUs were signed with UK universities.

title: Disciplines — History
content: In 2010, new disciplines like Law, Political Science, Urdu, Management Sciences, and Art & Design were introduced.

title: Renaming — History
content: The university was renamed from Frontier Women University to Shaheed Benazir Bhutto Women University through a legal amendment in 2010.

title: Higher Studies — History
content: In 2012, MS programs and MPhil leading to PhD in Economics, Computer Science, and Management Sciences were introduced under the KPK Universities Act 2012.

title: Growth — History
content: By 2012, the university had 4600 students in 18 departments and 16 affiliated colleges with over 5000 students.

title: Infrastructure — History
content: The university built academic blocks, hostels, administration block, and IT infrastructure including a high-speed network and wireless system.

title: Ranking — History
content: The university was ranked 9th by HEC among 27 new universities in Pakistan despite security and infrastructure challenges.

title: Gpa — General
content: SBBWU GPA calculation: GPA = sum of (Grade Point x Credit Hours) for all courses in a semester, divided by total credit hours attempted. CGPA is the same calculation across all semesters cumulatively. Grade scale is 1-4 with 85%+ = A (4.0), 70-84% = B (3.0-3.9), 60-69% = C (2.0-2.9), 50-59% = D (1.0-1.9), below 50% = F. title: Bs — Academic Concepts
content: A BS (Bachelor of Science) is an undergraduate degree that provides students with specialized knowledge and skills in a particular academic field. At SBBWU, BS programs are offered in various disciplines, including Computer Science, Bioinformatics, Biotechnology, Biochemistry, Microbiology, Chemistry, Mathematics, Statistics, Physics, Economics, Psychology, Political Science, English, Urdu, Islamiyat, Botany, Zoology, Geography, Education, and other fields.

title: Ms — Academic Concepts
content: MS (Master of Science) and MPhil (Master of Philosophy) are postgraduate degrees that provide advanced knowledge, specialized study, and research experience in a particular academic field. At SBBWU, MS and MPhil programs are offered in various disciplines, including Computer Science, Bioinformatics, Biochemistry, Microbiology, Chemistry, Economics, Education, Islamiyat, Mathematics, Political Science, Psychology, Statistics, Urdu, Zoology, Physics, and other fields, depending on the approved programs and admission session.

title: Phd — Academic Concepts
content: A PhD (Doctor of Philosophy) is the highest academic degree and is primarily focused on advanced research and the creation of new knowledge in a specific field. PhD students normally conduct original research, prepare a research thesis or dissertation, and defend their research according to the university's requirements. SBBWU offers PhD programs in various disciplines, including Computer Science, Biochemistry, Bioinformatics, Chemistry, Economics, Islamiyat, Mathematics, Management Sciences, Microbiology, Psychology, Statistics, Urdu, Zoology, and other approved fields.

title: Associate Degree — Academic Concepts
content: An Associate Degree is an undergraduate-level qualification that is generally completed in two years and provides foundational knowledge in a specific academic field. It may prepare students for employment or further education, depending on the applicable academic requirements. At SBBWU, Associate Degree programs are available through affiliated colleges in selected disciplines, subject to the programs approved and offered by the respective college.

title: Undergraduate — Academic Concepts
content: An undergraduate program is a program of study pursued before postgraduate education. It normally includes bachelor's degree programs and other equivalent undergraduate qualifications. At SBBWU, undergraduate education includes BS programs and other approved undergraduate programs offered by the university and its affiliated colleges.

title: Graduate — Academic Concepts
content: A graduate program is an advanced academic program pursued after completion of an undergraduate degree. Graduate-level education may include master's and doctoral studies and can involve advanced coursework, specialized study, research, or a combination of these. At SBBWU, advanced academic programs include MS, MPhil, and PhD programs in various disciplines.

title: Postgraduate — Academic Concepts
content: A postgraduate program is a program of study pursued after completion of an undergraduate degree. It generally includes master's-level and doctoral-level education and may focus on advanced academic study, professional specialization, or research. At SBBWU, postgraduate and advanced studies include MS, MPhil, and PhD programs in various academic disciplines.

title: Semester — Academic Concepts
content: A semester is an academic period during which students attend classes, complete coursework, take examinations, and earn academic credits. An academic year is commonly divided into two or more semesters. At SBBWU, academic programs are organized into semesters according to the university's academic calendar and the study plan of each program.

title: Credit Hour — Academic Concepts
content: A credit hour is a unit used to represent the amount of academic work assigned to a course. Each course carries a specific number of credit hours, and students must complete the required total credit hours of their degree program to graduate. At SBBWU, the credit hours assigned to courses are specified in the curriculum and study plan of each academic program.

title: Cgpa — Academic Concepts
content: CGPA (Cumulative Grade Point Average) represents a student's overall academic performance across the completed semesters of a degree program. It is calculated from the grade points earned in courses and their corresponding credit hours. At SBBWU, students' academic performance and CGPA are determined according to the university's applicable grading and academic regulations.

title: Core Course — Academic Concepts
content: A core course is a compulsory course that students must complete as part of their degree requirements. An elective course is a course that students may choose from a specified group of available courses according to the requirements of their academic program. At SBBWU, the core and elective courses for each degree are defined in the approved curriculum and study plan of the respective program.

title: Fyp — Academic Concepts
content: A Final Year Project (FYP) is an academic project completed by students as part of the requirements of certain undergraduate degree programs. It allows students to apply the knowledge and skills gained during their studies to a research, development, design, or practical problem. At SBBWU, the requirements and structure of the FYP depend on the relevant academic program and its approved curriculum.

title: Fyp — Academic Concepts
content: The semester or academic year in which BS students start their Final Year Project or research project depends on the approved curriculum and study plan of their specific program. At SBBWU, students should follow the project requirements and semester allocation specified by their department and academic program. The chatbot should provide a specific semester only when it is supported by the relevant official SBBWU curriculum or departmental information.

title: Fyp Duration — Academic Concepts
content: The duration of a Final Year Project or research project depends on the academic program, approved curriculum, and departmental requirements. A project may be completed within one or more semesters depending on the structure of the program. At SBBWU, the chatbot should provide the specific project duration only when it is supported by official information from the relevant department or academic program.

title: Research Project — Academic Concepts
content: A research project normally involves several stages, which may include selecting a research topic, identifying a research problem, preparing a project proposal, reviewing relevant literature, defining the research methodology, collecting or developing the required data or system, analyzing or evaluating the results, preparing the final report, and presenting or defending the project. The exact stages and requirements may vary according to the academic program and departmental guidelines at SBBWU.

title: Project Proposal — Academic Concepts
content: A project proposal is a formal document that describes a proposed research or development project. It generally explains the project title, background, problem statement, objectives, scope, proposed methodology, expected outcomes, and relevant references. A proposal helps the student and supervisor evaluate the feasibility and academic value of the proposed project. At SBBWU, proposal requirements may vary according to the department and academic program.

title: Research Supervisor — Academic Concepts
content: A research supervisor is a faculty member who guides a student during an academic research project, Final Year Project, thesis, or similar research work. The supervisor may help the student refine the topic, develop the research methodology, monitor progress, review academic work, and prepare for the final presentation or defense. At SBBWU, supervisor selection and responsibilities are subject to the rules and procedures of the relevant department and academic program.

title: Plagiarism — Academic Concepts
content: Plagiarism is the use of another person's words, ideas, data, research, or other intellectual work without proper acknowledgment or citation. In academic projects, students should properly cite sources, acknowledge the work of other researchers, and present their own work honestly. Plagiarism is considered a violation of academic integrity and may result in academic consequences according to the applicable university rules. SBBWU students should follow the university's academic integrity and plagiarism policies when preparing research projects, theses, and academic assignments.

title: Passing Marks — Passing Rules
content: A student must obtain at least 50% marks in each paper to pass.

title: Grade A — Grading
content: 85% and above corresponds to Grade A with GPA 4.0 and Excellent performance.

title: Grade B — Grading
content: 70 to 84% corresponds to Grade B with GPA between 3.0 and 3.9.

title: Grade C — Grading
content: 60 to 69% corresponds to Grade C with GPA between 2.0 and 2.9.

title: Grade D — Grading
content: 50 to 59% corresponds to Grade D with GPA between 1.0 and 1.9.

title: Fail — Grading
content: Marks below 50% correspond to Grade F which means fail.

title: Withdrawn — Grading
content: Grade W indicates a withdrawn course.

title: Incomplete — Grading
content: Grade I indicates an incomplete course.

title: Sgpa — Gpa
content: SGPA is calculated by dividing the sum of grade points multiplied by credit hours by total credit hours in a semester.

title: Cgpa — Gpa
content: CGPA is calculated by dividing the sum of grade points multiplied by credit hours of all semesters by total credit hours.

title: Rounding — Gpa
content: If the third decimal in GPA is 5 or more, it is rounded up.

title: Rounding — Gpa
content: If the third decimal in GPA is 4 or less, it is rounded down.

title: Withdrawn — Academic Rules
content: A withdrawn course is not counted as fail and is not included in GPA or CGPA calculation.

title: Incomplete — Academic Rules
content: An incomplete course is not included in GPA or CGPA calculation.

title: Evaluation — Thesis
content: Thesis or project evaluation is conducted by an external examiner appointed by the competent authority.

title: Viva — Thesis
content: The viva voce of thesis is conducted by the external examiner along with the supervisor and head of department.

title: Payment — Thesis
content: Honorarium is paid to examiners including the head of department for thesis evaluation.

title: Original Name — University History
content: SBBWU was first established as the Frontier Women University and was later renamed Shaheed Benazir Bhutto Women University.

title: Inauguration — University History
content: The SBBWU campus was inaugurated on 1st September 2004 by Akram Khan Durrani, the then Chief Minister of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (then called NWFP).

title: Legal Establishment — University History
content: SBBWU was formally created through the Frontier Women University Act 2004, which was passed by the Provincial Assembly of NWFP on 5th October 2004 and assented to by the Governor of NWFP on 7th February 2005. This is why some records list its established date as 2005.

title: Significance — University History
content: SBBWU holds the significance of being the first public-sector women's university in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (then NWFP).

title: Naming — University History
content: SBBWU is named in honor of Benazir Bhutto and other women who contributed to women's empowerment and the country's development.

title: Growth — University History
content: In 2010, SBBWU expanded with new departments — Law, Political Science, Urdu, Management Sciences, and Art & Design — along with an M.Phil program in Statistics, following the Frontier Women University (Amendment) Act, 2010.

title: Campuses — University History
content: Today, SBBWU has campuses in both Peshawar and Swabi, and is affiliated with the Higher Education Commission (HEC) of Pakistan.

title: First Vc — Administration
content: Prof. Dr. Syeda Farhana Jahangir was the first Vice Chancellor of Shaheed Benazir Bhutto Women University (SBBWU), Peshawar. She served during the university's early establishment and founding period.

title: Gold Medals — Convocation Awards

title: Chief Guest — Convocation Guests

title: Speech — Convocation Speeches
